title: hello-channel-whatsapp — a signed webhook, a customer, a reply (target: channel)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “A daemon that takes Meta Graph webhooks and replies on the WhatsApp Business endpoint.” Three env refs make it go — beat 2 pins the exact list the daemon enforces.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the tokens
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the Meta values and the API key for the boot beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec: an agent on a business number

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “Two lines. channel compiles a daemon — something that waits for customers, not a prompt.”

beats.label: Add the agent
beats.cue: “When a customer messages, reply concisely — 1 to 3 sentences.” That's the support voice.

beats.label: Give it one tool
beats.cue: “Ground answers in repo state” — read, and nothing else is even registered.

beats.label: Wire WhatsApp Business
beats.cue: Three env references: the number's id, the send token, and the app secret Meta signs with.

beats.label: Decide what a conversation is
beats.cue: sessionKey: user — one running conversation per customer, keyed by their phone number.

beats.label: Scope it before it's unattended
beats.cue: An unattended daemon can't stop to ask you — so what it may do is declared up front.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “All three Meta values lower to kind: env. Not one secret lands in the artifact.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target channel — phoneNumberId/accessToken/appSecret are {kind:"env"} refs

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, with no Meta token.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (4 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the spec env refs gate

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: “Adapter, gateway, session router, janitor, SIGTERM — a service, from 21 lines of YAML.”

beats.label: Find the boot gate
beats.cue: “PHONE_NUMBER_ID, ACCESS_TOKEN, APP_SECRET — it names all three and exits 2, before a single API call.”

verify.note: 6 matching lines (21, 23, 25, 26, 31, 32) — the required-env gate lowered from the spec's three env refs, ending in process.exit(2)

beats.label: Ask run to run it
beats.cue: “run is the cli/browser REPL. A channel is a daemon — the CLI names the shapes it takes.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `crewhaus run supports target: cli or browser (got "channel")`

beats.label: Boot the daemon with no secrets
beats.cue: “There's the gate, live: three Meta variables plus a provider key — and exit 2 until they're set.”
beats.command: env -u WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID -u WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN -u WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY bun live/dist/daemon.ts

verify.note: designed refusal — `[daemon] missing required env vars: WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID, WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN, WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; env -u scrubs what Setup sourced, so the gate fires either way

beats.label: Give the callback a public URL
beats.cue: [manual] Meta only calls a public HTTPS host: tunnel :3000, then set that host + /whatsapp/events as the app's callback URL.

verify.note: needs ngrok (or any tunnel) and a second terminal; the callback URL itself is set by hand in Meta's WhatsApp Business app dashboard — no CLI does it

beats.label: Boot the daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Three Meta values and an API key: it's on :3000, waiting for the callback.”

verify.note: needs WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID + WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN + WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET + Anthropic credentials; serves the gateway on PORT (default 3000)

beats.label: Find the conversation on disk
beats.cue: [manual] With the callback pointed here: message the business number, ⌃C the daemon, one transcript per customer.

verify.note: needs a human, a Meta-configured callback URL reaching this daemon, and a real keyed turn before the transcript exists

groups.title: One more thing · the gateway you didn't write

beats.label: Open the emitted gateway
beats.cue: “Nothing in the spec asked for this file — it's what target: channel means.”

beats.label: Read the two guards
beats.cue: “An unsigned request is a 401. The same message twice is a duplicate — not a second model call.”

verify.note: 4 lines — signature check (401) on both routes, then atomic idempotency-key dedup

beats.label: Read the session key
beats.cue: “sessionKey: user became a sha256 of adapter:workspace:user — stable across daemon restarts.”

verify.note: 5 lines — the sessionKey choice lowered into a deterministic sess_<16hex> id

beats.label: Ask the CLI to provision it
beats.cue: “provision automates Slack, Telegram and Discord. Meta's dashboard owns this one — it says so.”

verify.note: honest boundary — `whatsapp is configured but not supported by this command`; the callback URL is set in Meta's app dashboard
